title: Data Breach Response
description: You are handling a security incident inside breach_response/. Some folders and files are locked (read-only), so you must temporarily unlock them, do your work, and lock them back.
directoryTree:
breach_response/
├── evidence/
│   └── log_dump.txt
├── secure/
├── reports/
│   └── incident_summary.txt
└── classified.txt
preExistingNotes: classified.txt has no permissions (000) — do NOT touch it
actions: Give write permission to evidence/ (755), move evidence/ into secure/, then lock secure/evidence/ back to 555.
Give write permission to reports/incident_summary.txt (644), append 'Breach confirmed', then lock it back to 444.
Create secure/forensics_report.txt with the text 'Forensics Complete' and set its permissions to 600.
Unlock reports/incident_summary.txt (644), append 'Escalated to security team', and lock it back to 444.
hint: Start with: cd breach_response. Use chmod 755 before mv evidence secure, and chmod 644 before echo >> on incident_summary.txt.
solution:
cd breach_response
cp evidence/log_dump.txt log_dump.txt
chmod 755 evidence
mv evidence secure
chmod 555 secure/evidence
chmod 644 reports/incident_summary.txt
echo "Breach confirmed" >> reports/incident_summary.txt
chmod 444 reports/incident_summary.txt
echo "Forensics Complete" > secure/forensics_report.txt
chmod 600 secure/forensics_report.txt
chmod 644 reports/incident_summary.txt
echo "Escalated to security team" >> reports/incident_summary.txt
chmod 444 reports/incident_summary.txt

title: CLI + Git Release Pipeline v1
description: Set up release_v1/ with scripts and config, commit on a release branch, merge to main, and push.
actions: Create release_v1/bin/start.sh with 'echo running' and set its permissions to 755.
Create release_v1/config/prod.env with 'TOKEN=123' and set its permissions to 600.
Initialize Git, stage all files, and commit with 'Initial release_v1 setup'.
Create and switch to a new branch named 'release'.
Create release_v1/VERSION with 'v1.0', stage all files, and commit with 'Bump version'.
hint: Follow each numbered step in order: mkdir -p, echo >, chmod, git init, git add/commit, git checkout -b release, git checkout main, git merge release, git remote add, git push.
solution:
mkdir -p release_v1/bin release_v1/config
echo "echo running" > release_v1/bin/start.sh
chmod 755 release_v1/bin/start.sh
echo "TOKEN=123" > release_v1/config/prod.env
chmod 600 release_v1/config/prod.env
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial release_v1 setup"
git checkout -b release
echo "v1.0" > release_v1/VERSION
git add .
git commit -m "Bump version"
git checkout main
git merge release
git remote add origin https://github.com/NST/release_v1.git
git push -u origin main

Initialize Git, stage all files, and commit with 'Initial release_v7 setup'.
Create and switch to a new branch named 'release'.
Create release_v7/VERSION with 'v7.0', stage all files, and commit with 'Bump version'.
hint: Follow each numbered step in order: mkdir -p, echo >, chmod, git init, git add/commit, git checkout -b release, git checkout main, git merge release, git remote add, git push.
solution:
mkdir -p release_v7/bin release_v7/config
echo "echo running" > release_v7/bin/start.sh
chmod 755 release_v7/bin/start.sh
echo "TOKEN=123" > release_v7/config/prod.env
chmod 600 release_v7/config/prod.env
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial release_v7 setup"
git checkout -b release
echo "v7.0" > release_v7/VERSION
git add .
git commit -m "Bump version"
git checkout main
git merge release
git remote add origin https://github.com/NST/release_v7.git
git push -u origin main
